newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia cenbank warns producer price rise a threat.
newsitem.headline: Croatia cenbank warns producer price rise a threat.

text.p: Croatia's central bank warned on Thursday a 1.6 percent rise in November producer prices after a longer stable period could spur inflation, posing a threat to the economic stability.

"Since an increase of 2.8 percent was recorded in production materials, there are reasons to worry about an increased cost pressure on overall prices," the bank said in a statement released after the monthly board meeting.
It blamed delays in restructuring vital parts of the Croatian economy and monopolistic position of some companies in various market segments.
"Stricter monetary policy measures alone cannot be a solution for such sources of pressure," it added.
The bank pointed out that the retail prices went up only 0.5 percent and living costs 0.6 percent in November, their rise slowing down from October's 0.6 and 0.7 percent, respectively.
November retail prices were 3.5 percent and producer prices 1.7 percent higher year-on-year. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
